items.title: Victor Rendon interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, November 15, 2019 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: There was a guy named Gottschalk. ... And he was influenced by that, or he actually went to South America and died or something, if I’m correct. ... That’s my opinion from what I’ve read and listened to over the years.

ctx.x: And it talks a lot about the Caribbean influence. [scats] It has like what they called that cincio rhythm [scats] you could put it in clave. A lot of it has the [scats] that’s the cincio. [scat] It’s five notes. Cincio means cinco and that music came to New Orleans. And a lot of it came via Mexico, I didn’t know that, that there was like a family of teachers that came through New Orleans to teach and they were very influential in the early development of jazz, which I never knew. So I think that might be what he…
